The World Health Organization (WHO) and partners launched a global roadmap on hypertensive disorders in pregnancy, including pre-eclampsia, in a news item dated 8 October 2026.
The roadmap covers 2026 to 2035 and sets out coordinated actions on research, clinical guidance, access to medicines and diagnostics, implementation, advocacy and accountability.
The WHO says hypertensive disorders complicate an estimated 10 to 15% of pregnancies worldwide and are a leading cause of maternal and newborn deaths.
The roadmap highlights a gap in approved treatments: few medicines have been approved by regulators specifically to prevent or treat pre-eclampsia or eclampsia.

ledger.sentence: The WHO notes that many countries still lack reliable access to basic blood-pressure measurement, testing and essential medicines.
